recipes.title: Horn & Hardart Macaroni and Cheese
recipes.description: The Automat's most requested recipe, served daily to thousands. Rich, creamy, with a distinctive tang from dry mustard.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Butter a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until just al dente. Drain and set aside.
In a large saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in warm milk. Cook, stirring frequently, until sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon, about 8-10 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in cheese, mustard, salt, and pepper until cheese is completely melted.
Fold in cooked macaroni until evenly coated.
Transfer to prepared baking dish. Top with breadcrumbs if using.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden and bubbling. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.source: Horn & Hardart Archives, adapted from 1952 recipe card
recipes.story: Horn & Hardart's macaroni and cheese was served in thousands of portions daily. The secret was sharp cheddar and dry mustard, giving it a distinctive tang. When the last Automat closed in 1991, this recipe was thought lost until Marianne Hardart discovered it in family papers.

recipes.title: Automat Boston Baked Beans
recipes.description: Slow-baked for hours in the Automat's massive ovens, these beans became legendary for their deep, molasses-rich flavor.
instructions: Rinse beans and place in a large pot. Cover with water by 2 inches. Soak overnight, or quick-soak by boiling 2 minutes then letting stand 1 hour.
Drain beans. Return to pot with fresh water. Bring to boil, reduce heat, and simmer until beans are just tender, about 45 minutes. Drain, reserving cooking liquid.
Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Score salt pork in a crosshatch pattern. Place half at the bottom of a bean pot or Dutch oven.
Add beans and nestle onion quarters into them.
Whisk together molasses, brown sugar, mustard, salt, pepper, and 2 cups reserved bean liquid. Pour over beans.
Top with remaining salt pork. Add enough bean liquid to just cover beans.
Cover and bake for 5-6 hours, checking hourly and adding liquid if beans look dry.
Uncover for final 30 minutes to brown the top.
recipes.story: The Automat's bean pots held gallons and baked overnight in their massive ovens. Customers lined up early knowing the beans would be sold out by noon. This recipe captures that long, slow bake that made them unforgettable.

recipes.title: Creamy Automat Rice Pudding
recipes.description: Simple, homey, and utterly satisfying. The Automat served this cold in individual glass cups, topped with a dusting of nutmeg.
instructions: In a heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine rice, milk, and salt. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, until rice is very tender and mixture has thickened, about 40-45 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk egg yolks with cream and sugar.
Slowly whisk about 1 cup of hot rice mixture into the egg mixture to temper it.
Pour tempered eggs back into the pot, stirring constantly.
Cook over low heat, stirring, until pudding thickens further, about 5 minutes. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in vanilla and raisins if using.
Pour into serving dishes. Press plastic wrap directly onto surface to prevent skin.
Chill at least 2 hours. Dust with nutmeg before serving.
recipes.story: The glass-enclosed compartments of the Automat displayed these puddings like jewels. For a nickel, you'd turn the chrome knob and retrieve a cup of comfort. Many New Yorkers remember this as their introduction to dessert.

recipes.title: Automat Creamed Spinach
recipes.description: Silky smooth and deeply savory, this was the vegetable side that converted spinach skeptics.
instructions: If using fresh spinach, wash thoroughly and remove tough stems. Blanch in boiling salted water for 1 minute, then plunge into ice water. Drain and squeeze very dry.
If using frozen, thaw completely and squeeze out all moisture.
Roughly chop the spinach.
In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add shallots and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Sprinkle flour over the shallots and stir to combine. Cook 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in cream and milk. Cook until thickened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add spinach, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine and heat through.
Adjust seasoning and serve immediately.
recipes.story: The Automat's creamed spinach was so popular that it inspired countless steakhouse imitations. The secret was the shallots and fresh nutmeg, elevating a simple vegetable into something memorable.

recipes.title: Horn & Hardart Chicken Pot Pie
recipes.description: Individual pot pies with a flaky crust and rich, herb-flecked filling. The Automat's ultimate comfort food.
instructions: Poach chicken in broth until cooked through, about 20 minutes. Remove chicken, shred, and set aside. Reserve broth.
In a large pot, melt butter over medium heat. Add onion, celery, and carrots. Cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables and stir to coat. Cook 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in reserved broth and cream. Bring to simmer and cook until thickened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in shredded chicken, peas, thyme, salt, and pepper. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Divide filling among 6 individual ramekins or one 9x13 baking dish.
Cut puff pastry to fit over dishes. Place pastry on top and crimp edges. Cut small vents. Brush with egg wash.
Bake until pastry is golden and filling is bubbling, 25-30 minutes.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.story: These individual pot pies were assembled by the hundreds each morning. The Automat's version had a perfectly puffed crust you'd crack open to reveal the steaming, fragrant filling inside.

recipes.title: Automat Beef Stew
recipes.description: Hearty and warming, this stew fed generations of New Yorkers through cold winters.
instructions: Season beef with salt and pepper. Toss with flour to coat.
Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef in batches, about 3 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
Add onions to pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Add broth, Worcestershire, bay leaves, and thyme. Scrape up any browned bits.
Return beef to pot. Bring to boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 1 hour.
Add potatoes, carrots, and celery. Continue simmering until vegetables are tender and beef is very tender, about 45 minutes more.
Remove bay leaves. Adjust seasoning and serve.
recipes.story: On winter days, the line for beef stew stretched out the door. The Automat's version was thick, warming, and substantial enough to fuel a long day of work.

recipes.title: Automat Cod Fish Cakes
recipes.description: Crispy on the outside, fluffy within. A Friday staple at the Automat.
instructions: If using salt cod, soak in cold water for 24-48 hours, changing water several times. Drain.
Place cod in a pot, cover with cold water, and bring to simmer. Cook until fish flakes easily, about 10 minutes. Drain and flake, removing any bones.
Boil potatoes until tender. Drain, peel, and mash while hot.
Melt butter in a small pan. Cook onion until soft but not browned.
Combine fish, potatoes, onion, egg, parsley, and pepper. Mix well.
Shape into 8 patties about 3 inches across and 3/4 inch thick.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry fish cakes until golden brown, about 4 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels. Serve hot with lemon and tartar sauce.
recipes.story: Every Friday, the Automat's fish cakes disappeared within hours. Made fresh each morning, they were crispy, flaky, and always served piping hot.

recipes.title: Automat Meatloaf with Gravy
recipes.description: The ultimate diner meatloaf, served with rich brown gravy just like at the Automat.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soak breadcrumbs in milk for 5 minutes.
Combine beef, pork, onion, soaked breadcrumbs, eggs, ketchup, Worcestershire, salt, and pepper. Mix gently until just combined.
Shape into a loaf on a rimmed baking sheet or in a loaf pan.
Bake until internal temperature reaches 160°F (71°C), about 1 hour.
Let rest 10 minutes before slicing.
For gravy: Melt butter in a saucepan. Whisk in flour and cook 1 minute. Gradually add broth, whisking constantly. Simmer until thickened.
Serve meatloaf slices with gravy.
recipes.story: The Automat's meatloaf was comfort food perfection—moist, well-seasoned, and always served with a ladleful of rich gravy. It was the meal that reminded everyone of home.

recipes.title: Automat Coconut Custard Pie
recipes.description: One of the legendary pies displayed in the Automat's glass cases. Silky custard meets toasted coconut.
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Place pie crust in pan and crimp edges.
Toast 0.5 cup coconut in a dry skillet until golden. Set aside for topping.
Whisk eggs and sugar until smooth.
Heat milk and cream until steaming (not boiling). Slowly whisk into egg mixture.
Add vanilla, salt, and nutmeg.
Scatter remaining 1 cup coconut in pie crust.
Carefully pour custard over coconut.
Bake at 425°F for 15 minutes, then reduce to 350°F (175°C) and bake until custard is set but still jiggles slightly, about 30-35 minutes more.
Cool completely. Top with toasted coconut before serving.
recipes.story: The pie cases at the Automat were works of art. Behind their gleaming glass, coconut custard pie sat like edible treasure, waiting for someone to drop in their nickels.

recipes.title: Automat Swedish Meatballs
recipes.description: Tender meatballs in a silky cream gravy, served over egg noodles.
instructions: Soak breadcrumbs in milk for 5 minutes.
Combine beef, pork, soaked breadcrumbs, egg, onion, allspice, nutmeg, and salt. Mix gently.
Roll into 1-inch meatballs (about 40).
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet. Brown meatballs in batches. Remove and set aside.
Add remaining butter to skillet. Whisk in flour and cook 1 minute.
Gradually add broth, whisking constantly. Bring to simmer.
Stir in cream. Return meatballs to skillet.
Simmer until meatballs are cooked through and sauce is thickened, about 15 minutes.
Serve over buttered egg noodles.
recipes.story: New York's Swedish immigrant population helped make these meatballs an Automat staple. The cream gravy was the key—rich, smooth, and perfect for soaking into egg noodles.

recipes.title: Old-Fashioned Tapioca Pudding
recipes.description: Creamy, comforting, and studded with pearl tapioca. A forgotten classic from the Automat dessert case.
instructions: Soak tapioca in milk for 30 minutes.
Transfer to a saucepan. Add sugar and salt. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring frequently.
Cook, stirring constantly, until tapioca is translucent and mixture thickens, about 15 minutes.
Beat egg yolks in a small bowl. Slowly whisk in about 1 cup of hot tapioca mixture to temper.
Return tempered yolks to pot. Cook, stirring, for 2 more minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form. Fold into warm pudding.
Pour into serving dishes. Serve warm or chilled.
recipes.story: Tapioca pudding was comfort in a cup—the kind of old-fashioned dessert that reminded customers of their grandmothers' kitchens.

recipes.title: Automat Salisbury Steak
recipes.description: Seasoned beef patties smothered in rich onion gravy. Classic diner fare at its finest.
instructions: Combine beef, breadcrumbs, egg, minced onion, Worcestershire, salt, and pepper. Mix gently.
Form into 6 oval patties, about 3/4 inch thick.
Cook patties in a large skillet over medium-high heat, about 4 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
Add butter to skillet. Cook sliced onions until caramelized, about 15 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over onions and stir. Cook 1 minute.
Add broth and stir, scraping up browned bits. Simmer until thickened.
Return patties to skillet. Simmer in gravy for 10 minutes.
Serve patties smothered in onion gravy.
recipes.story: Named after 19th-century physician James Salisbury who promoted ground beef as health food, this dish became a diner staple. The Automat's version featured deeply caramelized onions.

recipes.title: Automat Apple Pie
recipes.description: The pie that launched a thousand nickels. Flaky crust, tender spiced apples, and that unmistakable Automat magic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Line a 9-inch pie plate with one round of dough.
Toss apples with sugars, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and lemon juice.
Pile apple mixture into crust. Dot with butter.
Top with second crust. Trim and crimp edges. Cut vents.
Brush with egg wash. Sprinkle with a little sugar.
Bake 20 minutes at 425°F, then reduce to 375°F (190°C) and bake until golden and bubbling, about 35-40 minutes more.
Cool at least 2 hours before slicing.
recipes.story: The Automat sold more apple pie than any other dessert. The secret was in the spice blend and letting the pie cool completely before cutting—a patience that made each slice perfect.

recipes.title: Automat Franks and Beans
recipes.description: A childhood favorite elevated to Automat standards. Sweet, savory, and utterly satisfying.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Cut hot dogs into 1-inch pieces.
Combine beans, ketchup, molasses, brown sugar, mustard, onion, Worcestershire, salt, and pepper in a baking dish.
Nestle hot dog pieces into the bean mixture.
Bake uncovered until bubbling and slightly thickened, about 45 minutes.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.story: Sometimes the simplest dishes are the most beloved. Franks and beans was the Automat's answer to the question: what's for lunch when you're nine years old?
